findings.title: Secret stored in a plaintext config file
findings.explanation: Plaintext secrets in config files are exposed to anyone with repository or host access.
findings.impact: Insecure configuration increases the impact of an otherwise limited exposure.
findings.remediation: Move secrets to an environment variable or a secrets manager.

findings.title: Secret stored in a plaintext config file
findings.explanation: Plaintext secrets in config files are exposed to anyone with repository or host access.
findings.impact: Insecure configuration increases the impact of an otherwise limited exposure.
findings.remediation: Move secrets to an environment variable or a secrets manager.

findings.title: Committed environment file
findings.explanation: A .env file is tracked in the repository with 2 populated value(s).
findings.impact: Environment files routinely carry credentials and are the most common leak vector.
findings.evidence: 2 populated keys, names only: API_KEY, SECRET_KEY
findings.remediation: Remove the file, add it to .gitignore, and rotate its contents.

findings.title: Hardcoded password assignment
findings.impact: Credential or sensitive configuration exposed in source.
findings.remediation: Read the value from an environment variable or a secrets manager.

findings.title: Hardcoded API key assignment
findings.impact: Credential or sensitive configuration exposed in source.
findings.remediation: Move the key to an environment variable or a secrets manager and rotate it.

findings.title: Shell command built by interpolation
findings.impact: Credential or sensitive configuration exposed in source.
findings.remediation: Pass arguments as a list and never through a shell; validate against an allowlist.

findings.title: Tainted data reaches SQL execution
findings.explanation: A user-controlled value flows from line 6 (request.args) to a SQL execution on line 9.
findings.impact: If the intermediate handling does not sanitise the value, this is exploitable. Confirm by reading the function.
findings.evidence: source: 'request.args' -> sink: SQL execution; variables: name
findings.remediation: Validate and sanitise the input at the boundary; use parameterised queries, argument lists, or context-aware escaping.

findings.title: Tainted data reaches shell execution
findings.explanation: A user-controlled value flows from line 13 (request.args) to a shell execution on line 16.
findings.impact: If the intermediate handling does not sanitise the value, this is exploitable. Confirm by reading the function.
findings.evidence: source: 'request.args' -> sink: shell execution; variables: cmd
findings.remediation: Validate and sanitise the input at the boundary; use parameterised queries, argument lists, or context-aware escaping.

findings.title: gitleaks: generic-api-key
findings.explanation: gitleaks detected a credential-shaped value in the working tree.
findings.impact: Exposed credential in a tracked or present file.
findings.remediation: Remove the value, rotate it, and read it from the environment.

findings.title: Debug mode enabled
findings.explanation: Debug mode leaks stack traces, environment details, and sometimes enables interactive consoles.
findings.impact: Insecure configuration increases the impact of an otherwise limited exposure.
findings.remediation: Disable debug mode in production configurations and builds.

findings.title: Container or pod runs as root
findings.explanation: Running as root increases the impact of any container escape.
findings.impact: Insecure configuration increases the impact of an otherwise limited exposure.
findings.remediation: Define a non-root USER and disable privilege escalation.

findings.title: Debug mode enabled
findings.impact: Credential or sensitive configuration exposed in source.
findings.remediation: Disable debug mode in production builds and deployments.

findings.title: Container runs as root
findings.impact: Credential or sensitive configuration exposed in source.
findings.remediation: Add a non-root USER instruction and drop capabilities.
